_doc: Grounded antibiotic FORMULARY — drug FACTS, not regimens. Each drug carries what it COVERS, CSF penetration, contraindications, a preference TIER (first-line=1 … reserve=5; grounded + editable), and a dose WINDOW (a feasible-interval: a per-dose floor for efficacy and a ceiling that shrinks as renal/interaction risks stack). The regimen is DERIVED from these facts by minimum-cost SET-COVER + exclusion + a dose-window solve (derive_regimen.py) — so it generalizes to any organism/drug without new rules, and the dose can go UNSAT when no safe-and-effective dose exists. Coverage facts from IDSA Tunkel 2004 + Sanford. The tier weights encode clinical preference among VALID options (also grounded/editable). The dose-window numbers are an ILLUSTRATIVE feasibility model, not validated PK/PD (mechanism demo, not a dosing tool). domain: empiric bacterial meningitis. Note s_pneumoniae_resistant = ceftriaxone-nonsusceptible pneumococcus (the reason vancomycin is added empirically).

combinations.source: IDSA Tunkel 2004 (via AAFP summary): for penicillin-/cephalosporin-resistant pneumococcus, vancomycin 'may be used in combination with a third-generation cephalosporin but should not be used alone (A-III)' — the spider REFUTED single-drug coverage and grounded this COMBINATION rule.
IDSA Tunkel 2004: vancomycin + a broad cephalosporin (cefepime) covers resistant pneumococcus in the nosocomial setting.

side_effects._doc: CC-4 side-effect / toxicity burden weight per drug (relative integer, 0=benign … 3=high-monitoring/toxicity). Feeds the COST+SIDE-EFFECT objective minimize(w_cost·tier + w_tox·side_effects): a cheap-but-toxic drug can lose to a pricier-but-safer one when w_tox>0. AUTHORED-DEBT — illustrative clinical estimates pending CC-4b spider grounding (FDA label adverse-event / monitoring burden); not validated tox data. Default objective weights are (w_cost=1, w_tox=0), which reproduces the tier-only set-cover exactly, so this layer is inert until a chart/policy raises w_tox.

vancomycin.dose_penalty_source: FDA vancomycin label (DailyMed 75a6a873): renal dysfunction + concomitant nephrotoxins lower the safe ceiling — DIRECTION grounded in dose-window-grounding.json (dose_penalty_vancomycin_renal, dose_penalty_vancomycin_nephrotoxin); the per-kg magnitudes stay the illustrative feasibility model
vancomycin.source: IDSA Tunkel 2004 (empiric vancomycin for resistant pneumococcus)

cefepime.dose_penalty_source: FDA cefepime label (DailyMed be5f8ca6): adjust dose at CrCl <= 60 mL/min, neurotoxicity if unadjusted in renal impairment — DIRECTION grounded in dose-window-grounding.json (dose_penalty_cefepime_renal); the per-kg magnitude stays the illustrative feasibility model

aztreonam.source: Monobactam; safe in penicillin allergy (no cross-reactivity)

tmp_smx.source: TMP-SMX for Listeria when ampicillin contraindicated
